evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context Layer 3 review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-RM9.spec.ts (committed b9553cc37d, unchanged); my own bare bun test run: 4 pass, 0 fail, 50 expect() calls. Given: the test writes a temporary blend spec folder and loads it with the real Blend.load (no failures) and TaskCommand.plan; it asserts T2 after [T1], T3 after [T2], S1 needs [T3], plus T4 after [T1], T5 after [T4, T2], T6 after [T2, T4]; before the failure T1 builds and every dependant waits with no cause (waitingOn T3 = [T2], S1 = [T3]). When: exactly one engine.apply of task.failed T1. Then T2 blocked by T1 and T3 blocked by T2 in the same fold step: T1 failed; T2 blockedBy {T1, failed}; T3 blockedBy {T2, blocked}; the history entries added by this one apply are waiting->blocked with reasons 'blocked by T1: failed' and 'blocked by T2: blocked', T2 before T3. S1 blocked by T3: blockedBy {T3, blocked}, one added history entry with its reason after T3's, and TaskStatus.project carries the cause and reason; the run then ends failed. Two dead dependencies named first in dependency order: T2 and T4 both become blocked in the one microstep; T5 (after [T4, T2]) names T4, not T2, so the choice follows dependency order and not id or region order; T6 (after [T2, T4]) names T2; history and status projection agree. I checked machine.ts: DEAD = [needs_human, budget_exhausted, failed, blocked] and blockRows emit rows in dependency order, so 'dead dependency' covers a blocked one, and the same-microstep construction is the only way two dependencies die at once. Every step is covered by discriminating assertions.
